notes.meaning: God showed Amos a basket of ripe summer fruit. In Hebrew, the word for summer fruit sounds almost identical to the word for the end. This showed that Israel was fully ripe for judgment, and God would no longer hold back His punishment.

other.label: Catholic
other.view: The old Latin Bible used by the Catholic Church reads the basket as a hook for pulling down fruit. Jerome explained it as God drawing the time of captivity closer.

notes.meaning: The songs in the palaces or shrines will suddenly change into wailing and cries of despair. An attacking enemy will leave so many dead bodies that the survivors will fling them out in stunned silence. Sin can quickly turn worldly celebrating into quiet heartbreak.

Amos warns the wealthy leaders who were crushing poor and helpless people under their feet. They were treating needy families like prey to be swallowed up and driven away. God watches closely whenever the powerful mistreat the weak.

The merchants observed holy days like the Sabbath and the New Moon, but they hated having business pause. They could not wait for worship to end so they could cheat customers with undersized grain baskets and heavy silver weights. True worship cannot live alongside a heart that loves dishonest gain.

The rich trapped poor families in debt until they could buy people as slaves for the price of a cheap pair of sandals. They even gathered worthless grain scraps off the floor and sold them to hungry buyers. God hates cruelty that treats human beings like cheap property.

The Lord makes a solemn oath by Himself, who is the true glory of Jacob. He promises that He will never overlook or forget any of their greedy acts. People may try to ignore their wrong choices, but God keeps a faithful record.

other.label: Catholic
other.view: The old Latin Bible reads it as God swearing against Jacob's pride, so the phrase points to Israel's arrogance.

notes.meaning: The land itself will shake with grief because of the evil done in it. God compares the coming ruin to the Nile River, which rises up in floodwaters and then sinks back down. Even nature trembles when a nation rejects God's justice.

God says He will make the sun go down at noon and darken the earth during broad daylight. This pictures sudden terror and ruin overtaking a proud people when they think everything is secure. Earthly safety means nothing without God's protection.

differ.view: The sun setting at noon is understood as a poetic picture of sudden national ruin striking at the height of prosperity.
The noon darkness pictures the political collapse of the northern kingdom during its final civil wars and invasions.
This verse is read as a direct prophecy pointing ahead to the three hours of darkness when Jesus died on the cross.

other.label: Catholic and Orthodox
other.view: Ancient church teachers often saw the midday darkness as a prophetic sign pointing to the darkness during the crucifixion of Christ.

notes.meaning: God will change joyful religious feasts into deep mourning and festive music into funeral crying. The people will put on scratchy goat-hair cloth called sackcloth and shave their heads in sorrow. The grief will be as terrible as losing an only son, leaving the country in bitter ruin.

The Lord warns that a famine is coming, but not one of physical bread or water. It will be a famine of hearing the words of the Lord. When people repeatedly reject God's truth, losing His guidance is the most severe punishment of all.

differ.view: The famine means God actively takes away His prophets and silences His revelation because the people refused to obey Him.
The famine describes people losing their spiritual ability to hear and understand God after hardening their own hearts.

notes.meaning: Desperate people will stagger from the Dead Sea to the Mediterranean and search from north to east trying to find a word from God. Even though they look all over the land, they will not find it. Seeking God only out of panic without genuine repentance will not bring answers.

Even the healthiest young women and strong young men will faint from thirst on that day. Physical strength cannot keep anyone alive when spiritual life is completely cut off. Human vigor will always fail without the strength God supplies.

Judgment will fall on those who take oaths in the name of the golden calves at Samaria and Dan, or the false shrine at Beersheba. Because they placed their trust in idols, they will collapse and never rise again. Trusting in anything other than the true and living God leads to final ruin.
